BA.rationale: Boeing's franchise is world-class — a co-duopolist with Airbus, a $682B+ backlog, and a high-margin Global Services segment (18.1% operating margin). The Q1 2026 results show genuine early-stage stabilization: revenue +14% YoY, net income near breakeven (-$7M vs. -$612M prior quarter), operating income positive at $448M, equity restored to +$5.99B from negative territory, and debt reduced by ~$6B. The China aircraft deal (200 planes announced 2026-05-16) and secular defense spending tailwinds ($960B+ DoD budget) provide credible near-term catalysts. However, the financial model remains fragile: operating cash flow turned negative again in Q1 2026 (-$179M), BCA operating margin is still -6.1%, leverage is extreme at 7.84x D/E, and the 1.3% earnings yield against a 4.57% risk-free rate means the market is pricing in a recovery that is barely underway. At 76.5x P/E and 28.9x P/B, there is no valuation cushion if execution falters. The Spirit AeroSystems integration adds ~$1B cash drag in 2026. The score reflects a high-quality franchise in early recovery that is fairly-to-slightly-richly priced, with a modest positive bump from the China deal catalyst — but not enough to overcome the thin margin of safety on fundamentals and valuation.
